name: MediaFast
tagline: Hosted media pipeline: upload files, transcode and optimize them, serve them fast over URLs.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of a media pipeline is unglamorous and well trodden: accept an upload, hand it to ffmpeg or sharp, cache the output, serve it behind a stable URL. An agent can stand that up in a weekend and it will genuinely work for one person's blog, app, or side project. What it will not do is match the boring parts that cost real money: edge delivery, cold start latency, every weird codec a phone camera produces, and a queue that does not fall over when someone uploads a two hour video. Details of the hosted product are unverified here, so treat the price and plan shape as unknown rather than as a comparison. If your traffic is small and your inputs are predictable, self hosting is fine; if either changes, you are now running infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: A local service that takes uploads, runs ffmpeg and sharp transforms on demand, caches the results on disk, and serves them from signed URLs.
requirements: A machine or VPS with ffmpeg installed and disk to spare
Node 20 and basic comfort with a terminal
A reverse proxy plus TLS if you want it reachable from the internet
Patience for codec errors that are technically your fault
whatYouLose: Edge caching, so your first byte comes from wherever your box lives
Battle tested handling of malformed and exotic input files
Autoscaling when someone drops a huge video into your queue
Usage dashboards, alerting, and someone else carrying the pager
Drop in SDKs and framework integrations you would otherwise not think about
moatNotes: The moat is not the ffmpeg invocation, it is the delivery layer and the thousand input files that break naive pipelines.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because media is the one part of a product where doing it yourself shows. Users notice a slow first frame, a broken thumbnail, or a phone upload that silently failed, and each of those is a separate afternoon of debugging codecs you did not want to learn about. Paying a service converts an ongoing infrastructure chore into a line item, and for anything with real traffic the edge delivery alone is hard to replicate on one box.
notes: Product specifics here are unverified, so the build is judged on the generic media pipeline it appears to be.
prompt:
Build a self hosted media processing and delivery service for a single owner. No SaaS accounts, no telemetry, no cloud dependencies.

Stack, non negotiable: Node 20 with TypeScript, Fastify for HTTP, better-sqlite3 for metadata, sharp for images, ffmpeg called via child_process for audio and video, local disk for storage. No Docker required to run, but include a Dockerfile.

Layout: /src for server code, /storage/originals, /storage/derived, /data/app.db, .env for secrets.

Features in scope:
1. POST /upload accepts multipart uploads, streams to /storage/originals under a content hashed key, records mime type, size, duration and dimensions in SQLite, returns the asset id.
2. GET /a/:id/:transform serves a derived file. Transform grammar is a compact string, for example w_800,h_600,fit_cover,q_80,f_webp for images and preset_720p, preset_audio_mp3, thumb_at_5s for video.
3. Derivatives are generated on first request, written to /storage/derived, and served from cache on every subsequent request. Return correct Content-Type, ETag, Cache-Control and support HTTP range requests for audio and video.
4. A simple in process job queue with a concurrency cap so two large transcodes never run at once. Requests for a pending derivative get a 202 with a retry hint, or block briefly for cheap image work.
5. Signed URLs: HMAC over asset id plus transform plus expiry, secret from .env. Unsigned requests are rejected unless PUBLIC_MODE is true.
6. A tiny HTML admin page listing assets with thumbnails, upload form, delete button, and disk usage. Protected by a bearer token from .env.
7. CLI script to reprocess or purge all derivatives.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, billing, multi tenancy, CDN or multi region replication, live streaming, DRM, AI tagging.

Correctness requirements: reject uploads over MAX_UPLOAD_MB, validate real mime type by sniffing bytes not the filename, never shell interpolate user input into ffmpeg args, time out any ffmpeg job past FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_SEC and record the failure with stderr.

.env keys: PORT, STORAGE_DIR, DB_PATH, SIGNING_SECRET, ADMIN_TOKEN, PUBLIC_MODE, MAX_UPLOAD_MB, FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_SEC, TRANSCODE_CONCURRENCY. Ship a .env.example.

Tests with vitest: transform string parsing, signature verification including expiry, cache hit path, and a rejected oversized upload.

README: install ffmpeg, run dev, curl examples for upload and for a signed transform URL, and a short note on putting Caddy or nginx in front for TLS.
